funds.directEquityBasis: BCI's audited 2025 program statements state that the Program primarily invests directly in privately held companies and report C$24.531 billion of direct private equity investments at December 31, 2025. The qualifying strategy is direct core infrastructure and renewable-resources equity; listed infrastructure, private infrastructure debt, and external-fund investments are complementary exposures within the broader program.

northAmericaQualification.rationale: BCI stated on April 21, 2026 that its Infrastructure & Renewable Resources program has been a shareholder in Global Container Terminals since 2017 and continues to support the Canadian container-terminal operator.

snapshot.investmentStrategy: Global core infrastructure and renewable-resources program focused primarily on direct investments in privately held essential-service businesses and tangible real assets, generally through meaningful positions with governance rights and anticipated multi-decade holding periods; listed infrastructure, private infrastructure debt, and selective external-fund investments complement the direct portfolio.

evidence.title: Infrastructure & Renewable Resources — Overview
evidence.evidenceLabel: Current program mandate, AUM date, sectors, and geographic footprint
evidence.evidenceSummary: BCI identifies I&RR as a $36.5 billion global program that invests primarily in core infrastructure and renewable resources, targets privately held assets with meaningful governance rights and holding periods exceeding 20 years, names its principal sectors, includes North America in its asset distribution, and states that program assets are valued annually at December 31, 2025.

evidence.title: Infrastructure & Renewable Resources Program — Combined Financial Statements, December 2025
evidence.evidenceLabel: Audited program identity, formation, structure, and direct-equity exposure
evidence.evidenceSummary: The audited statements say the Infrastructure Program and Renewable Resource Program were consolidated in 2020 to create I&RR, that the Program moved to Open Participation in 2021, that it primarily invests directly in privately held companies, and that direct private equity investments were C$24.531 billion at December 31, 2025. They also state that the combined Program is not itself a legal entity and list its constituent investment entities.

evidence.title: BCI Infrastructure & Renewable Resources named 10th-largest institutional infrastructure investor worldwide
evidence.evidenceLabel: Current C$36.5 billion AUM and regional deployment
evidence.evidenceSummary: BCI reports that I&RR AUM grew to C$36.5 billion, identifies the figure as AUM rather than commitments or a close, and names North America, Europe, Asia, and select emerging markets as current portfolio regions. The source gives no USD equivalent, so no USD amount or FX conversion is recorded.

evidence.title: Gateway to growth: GCT and Canada's West Coast port expansion strategy
evidence.evidenceLabel: Current Canadian holding attributed to I&RR
evidence.evidenceSummary: BCI states that the I&RR program has been a shareholder in Global Container Terminals since 2017 and continues to support the Canadian operator of GCT Deltaport and GCT Vanterm at the Port of Vancouver.

funds.repoDispositionRationale: FUND-030 is the same BCI program, but current primary materials use the program name, report C$36.5 billion expressly as AUM, provide no source-stated USD equivalent, date the current asset data to December 31, 2025, document the 2020 consolidation and an ongoing Open Participation program structure, and support updated sector, regional, and source fields. The snapshot structure is normalized to Evergreen because Open Participation is not an available repository structure enum.

excludedCandidates.rationale: BCI describes this as a dedicated investment-grade private-credit strategy investing in corporate credit and asset-backed financing. Its primary North American and European focus does not cure the absence of direct infrastructure equity.

unresolvedConflicts.subject: Infrastructure & Renewable Resources Program size measures
unresolvedConflicts.issue: BCI's July 2026 program update reports C$36.5 billion of AUM, while the audited December 2025 combined statements report C$35.337 billion of program net assets and C$35.404 billion of investments. The public sources do not reconcile these differently defined measures.
unresolvedConflicts.recommendedResolution: Retain C$36.5 billion only with the AUM label and do not substitute audited net assets or investments; obtain BCI's AUM-to-net-assets reconciliation before comparing these measures.

unresolvedConflicts.subject: Renewable Resources Investment Fund constituent status
unresolvedConflicts.issue: The 2024 program statements disclosed an intention to wind up the Renewable Resources Investment Fund after December 31, 2024, with the wind-up date unconfirmed. The 2025 program statements still list that fund among the investment entities comprising I&RR but do not expressly confirm whether the wind-up occurred.
unresolvedConflicts.recommendedResolution: Obtain BCI confirmation of the constituent fund's legal wind-up status if internal pooled entities are maintained in a separate legal-vehicle repository; this does not alter the one-row program-level census.

notes: One current qualifying direct-equity infrastructure program was identified; no conventional third-party fund series was identified.

The 2025 audited statements combine Bolsena Fund, Bolsena (Australia) Fund, Bolsena (Public) Fund, Renewable Resources Investment Fund, Orto (S-NPC) Fund, and various structured entities and individual investments; these were reviewed as internal constituents and not double-counted.
Global Container Terminals was verified as a current Canadian holding specifically attributed to the I&RR program.
The current Investment Grade Private Credit Fund was excluded because it is a credit strategy rather than direct infrastructure equity.

The regional taxonomy records Asia as Asia-Pacific and represents the program's expressly global footprint, including unspecified select emerging markets, with the allowed Global enum rather than assigning unsupported emerging-market subregions.
No essential primary source remained inaccessible.
